proves.claim: proofCounter keeps no prepared statement alive after its connection closes.

verify.proof.counter-release.why: A live statement kept the database file open and blocked cleanup.

proves.claim: evidence uses exact citations in tracked visible tests, and stage precedence follows sign-offs.

verify.evidence.citations.why: Loose citation matching let a clause count as proven without a real test.

proves.claim: an accept whose reviewed trunk is not an ancestor of main is judged from the merge base with the same overlap rule.

verify.freshness.trunk-merge-base.why: A trunk off main was wrongly judged stale or fresh.

proves.claim: each failure cause of the freshness check has its own reason text.

verify.freshness.reasons.why: One shared reason hid which check failed.

proves.claim: machine acceptance gives the accept move a real notBuilder check and passes it for a seat-built item.

verify.machine.not-builder.why: Machine acceptance once skipped the builder check.

proves.claim: machine acceptance refuses NOT_SUBMITTED for an item that left submitted.

verify.machine.not-submitted.why: An accept recorded on an item that was no longer submitted.

proves.claim: machine acceptance refuses NOT_SUBMITTED on the live row when the item leaves submitted after the precheck.

verify.machine.not-submitted-live.why: A race between the precheck and the write let a stale accept through.

proves.claim: two branches that each add a plan shard row and a data-read row compose in both orders on review retry.

verify.review.plan-compose.why: Review retry refused a merge that composes cleanly.

proves.claim: a row edited differently on both sides still refuses MERGE_CONFLICT on review retry.

verify.review.plan-conflict.why: Composition must never hide a true conflict.

proves.claim: main adding a far-away registry entry leaves the reviewed change fresh.

verify.freshness.far-registry-entry.why: Item #2896: unrelated registry growth made verdicts stale.

proves.claim: a conflicting or hunk-changing main edit keeps the verdict stale.

verify.freshness.conflicting-edit.why: Item #2896: freshness must still catch a real change.

proves.claim: two items adding registry entries in sequence both stay fresh.

verify.freshness.sequential-entries.why: Item #2896: the second landing made the first verdict stale.

proves.claim: main editing a nearby line that only changes hunk context leaves the reviewed change fresh.

verify.freshness.nearby-context.why: A context-only change made verdicts stale.

proves.claim: a verified item whose reviewed trunk is an ancestor of main is fresh, not STALE_VERDICT.

verify.freshness.ancestor-fresh.why: Ancestor trunks were refused as stale.

proves.claim: the ancestor check runs through the Git adapter, so a trunk on main raises no ReferenceError.

verify.freshness.ancestor-adapter.why: A missing adapter import crashed the check.

proves.claim: a verdict projector given a derived reader returns the reader state for an answered item, null included, with no computation.

verify.freshness.derived-reader.why: show reads verdict freshness from the derived-state table instead of Git.

proves.claim: an item the derived reader answers undefined for is computed as before, and a projector without a reader is unchanged.

verify.freshness.derived-fallback.why: A table gap must fall back to computing, never to a wrong answer.

proves.claim: ancestryStatus spawns at most 3 git processes for 1,038 verified items with unchanged answers.

verify.freshness.batched-git.why: One git process per item made the check too slow.

proves.claim: an accept on a submit composition commit goes STALE_VERDICT when main changes a reviewed file and stays fresh otherwise, as for a builder merge commit.

verify.freshness.composed-stale.why: The composed submit must keep the review bound to the files it covered.

proves.claim: with submit.composeAsObject on, a stale re-review checks a fresh object composition of current main and the head, and the STALE_VERDICT text never asks for a main merge.

verify.freshness.composed-re-review.why: A builder merges main only on a real conflict; the re-review composes main itself.

proves.claim: with submit.composeAsObject off, the STALE_VERDICT text and the re-review refusal are unchanged.

verify.freshness.composed-off.why: New behaviour ships behind a default-off setting.

proves.claim: with landing.composedEquality on, an item reopened by a landing re-proof red keeps its accepted verdict when main changed no file its review covered.

verify.freshness.reprove-red-kept.why: The review stays bound; a re-proof red is the tree's fault, not the review's.

proves.claim: a reopened item's verdict is withdrawn STALE_VERDICT, naming file and main commit, when main changed a file the review covered.

verify.freshness.reprove-red-stale.why: Only a changed reviewed file may cost a re-review.

proves.claim: with the setting off a reopened item's verdict is not kept, as today.

verify.freshness.reprove-red-off.why: New behaviour ships behind a default-off setting.

proves.claim: a merge conflict the injected residualConflicts port reports resolved keeps the accept fresh; files or no port leave it STALE_VERDICT.

verify.freshness.mechanical-port.why: The freshness door stays light, so the mechanical merge is a port, not an import.

proves.claim: with verify.frozenTests unset or false, a changed named test file is accepted.

verify.frozen.setting-off.why: The frozen-test refusal ships behind a default-off setting.

proves.claim: with verify.frozenTests true, a changed file is refused with TEST_HASH_CHANGED.

verify.frozen.setting-on.why: The setting must actually turn the refusal on.

proves.claim: the frozen hash of each named test file is recorded whatever the setting.

verify.frozen.hash-recorded.why: Turning the setting on later needs hashes already recorded.

proves.claim: only existing test files the criterion names are hashed.

verify.hash.named-only.why: Hashing unnamed or missing files froze the wrong content.

proves.claim: a hash already frozen is kept, not read again.

verify.hash.kept.why: Re-reading let a changed file replace its own frozen hash.

proves.claim: a builder edit is a change, while identical or main-supplied content is not.

verify.hash.change.why: Main-supplied content must not count as a builder edit.

proves.claim: the refusal names the file, and only a person ruling on that exact content lifts it.

verify.hash.ruling.why: Only the person may change a frozen test.

proves.claim: a bar frozen without hashes freezes nothing.

verify.hash.no-hashes.why: Older bars have no hashes and must not refuse.

proves.claim: a named test file the head adds is recorded with its seat and family, and an unchanged one is not.

verify.author.recorded.why: The author record is needed for the author and reviewer split.

proves.claim: a file already recorded at this content is not recorded twice, and a changed one is.
the newest author record per file is the one show prints.
a second loaded copy of the worker front door keeps its own process state.

verify.advance.copy-state.why: Shared module state leaked handles between copies.

proves.claim: the runner move preserves strict review for every strict planned source.

verify.advance.strict-review.why: A runner move once dropped strict review.

proves.claim: a verify accept with a build item free and no review ready returns the idle result no eligible review work.

verify.post-move.accept-never-claims-bui.why: A reviewer seat auto-claimed build items after every verdict.

proves.claim: a verify accept with a review ready still reserves that review.

verify.post-move.accept-still-reserves-r.why: A reviewer seat auto-claimed build items after every verdict.

proves.claim: a submit hand-off still takes the next build item through the same call.

verify.post-move.submit-handoff-unchange.why: A reviewer seat auto-claimed build items after every verdict.

proves.claim: queue and status find file collisions through a path index and match the all-pairs answer.

verify.queue.path-index.why: All-pairs collision search was too slow.

proves.claim: queue on a 3,000-item fixture runs in under 200 ms.

verify.queue.speed.why: Queue speed regressed with board size.

proves.claim: every verify-cell test has a stable ID and exactly one complete record, and no record is orphaned.

verify.registry.complete.why: Tests keyed by path rekey on every move; IDs and records make each test a bar.

proves.claim: with verify.testAuthorSplit unset, a test file the submitting seat changed is accepted.

verify.authorsplit.setting-off.why: The author split ships behind a default-off setting.

proves.claim: with verify.testAuthorSplit true, an item whose test file the submitting seat changed is refused with TEST_AUTHOR_SAME_SEAT.

verify.authorsplit.same-seat.why: The strict option needs a separate test author.

proves.claim: with verify.testAuthorSplit true, a different recorded author at the same content hash is accepted.

verify.authorsplit.other-author.why: A separate author must satisfy the split.

proves.claim: with tests.registryStrict off the registry check names an unregistered test in its report and passes.

verify.registry.report-names-file.why: A hard failure blocked ordinary work before the registry rule was approved.

proves.claim: with tests.registryStrict on the registry check fails an unregistered test and names its file.

verify.registry.strict-fails.why: The person needs a switch that makes the registry rule binding.

proves.claim: a review released as FAMILY or TOO_LARGE is not offered to the same reviewer again until the item is resubmitted

verify.io-review-routing.family-and-size.why: Waiting out a cooldown never fixed a wrong family or an oversize review, so the reviewer cycled the same offer (audit 4 Nov, #8922).

proves.claim: a review released as BAR or INFRA keeps the timed cooldown and ends after it

verify.io-review-routing.bar-and-infra-k.why: The timed cooldown stays for reasons waiting can fix (#8922).

proves.claim: below the review-reason engine a FAMILY release keeps the timed cooldown

verify.io-review-routing.old-engine-keep.why: A replay under an older engine must keep its recorded behaviour (#8922).

proves.claim: with the variable unset a file board writes proof counters to the derived database and board_meta holds none.

verify.proof.derived-default.why: The derived database was off unless opted in, so every board kept writing board_meta rows.

proves.claim: proof stats read from the derived database equal the totals board_meta gives with the variable 0.

verify.proof.derived-totals.why: A derived default that read different totals would change every stat.

proves.claim: an in-memory board has no file, so it keeps its proof counters in board_meta.

verify.proof.derived-memory-board.why: A default-on derived database must not break boards without a file.

proves.claim: with the variable 0 a file board makes no derived database and keeps its rows in board_meta.

verify.proof.derived-off.why: The off switch must still restore the old storage.

proves.claim: writeDerived prepares its upsert once per board connection.

verify.proof.derived-prepare-once.why: Preparing per call made a replay on a file board far slower.

proves.claim: sealedFallbackMain returns the submitted policy commit when no reuse, re-review, companion digest or effective head decides, whatever the check.

verify.io-reuse.sealed-fallback-no-check.why: An item with an empty frozen check was denied the sealed-move fallback.

proves.claim: sealedFallbackMain returns null when reused.ids, reReview, companionDigest or effectiveHead is set.

verify.io-reuse.sealed-fallback-guards.why: The fallback must never override a reuse, re-review, companion digest or effective head.

proves.claim: a numbered criterion whose clause text holds digit-period prose gives one clause numbered 1 with no leading marker and its kind.

verify.review-packet.numbered-clause-wit.why: Without it a bar with digit-period prose showed more clauses than the frozen bar held, so accept --read numbers stopped matching.

proves.claim: a three-clause numbered criterion with digit-period prose gives exactly three packet clauses numbered 1 to 3.

verify.review-packet.three-clauses-with-.why: Without it a bar with digit-period prose showed more clauses than the frozen bar held, so accept --read numbers stopped matching.

proves.claim: a free-text criterion with no leading number still splits at sentence ends.

verify.review-packet.free-text-still-spl.why: Without it a bar with digit-period prose showed more clauses than the frozen bar held, so accept --read numbers stopped matching.

proves.claim: clause 1: the same file digests and contract keys in a different order give the same key.

verify.logic-cell-key.order.why: A verdict reused under a key that moved with order or another cell would be wrong or never reused.

proves.claim: clause 2: changing one file digest of the cell, or one reached contract key, changes the key.

verify.logic-cell-key.change.why: A verdict reused under a key that moved with order or another cell would be wrong or never reused.

proves.claim: clause 3: changing a file of another cell, passed in no input, leaves this cell's key the same.

verify.logic-cell-key.other-cell.why: A verdict reused under a key that moved with order or another cell would be wrong or never reused.

proves.claim: clause 1: recordCellVerdict returns a new store and leaves the given store unchanged.

verify.logic-cell-verdicts.record-pure.why: A verdict reused under a key that moved, or one cell's record moving another's, would hide a changed cell.

proves.claim: clause 2: cellVerdict returns the recorded verdict for the same key, and null for a changed key of that cell or a cell never recorded.

verify.logic-cell-verdicts.same-key.why: A verdict reused under a key that moved, or one cell's record moving another's, would hide a changed cell.

proves.claim: clause 3: recording a verdict for one cell leaves every other cell's verdict as it was.

verify.logic-cell-verdicts.other-cells.why: A verdict reused under a key that moved, or one cell's record moving another's, would hide a changed cell.

proves.claim: a comparison worker started through a symlinked folder runs its body: a missing request exits non-zero naming it, as through the real path.

verify.comparison.entry-through-symlink.why: The tools snapshot sits under a symlinked temp root, and a plain path comparison made every worker exit 0 having run nothing.
